facts.raw_span: A woman in her 50s
morbid obesity
obstructive sleep apnea
3 days of fever with a temperature up to 39°C
anosmia
shortness of breath
Oxygen saturation of 85% on room air
coarse rales at the lung bases bilaterally
Nasopharyngeal swab positive by reverse transcriptase–polymerase chain reaction
Chest Radiography: Suggestive of bilateral multifocal pneumonia
Normal sinus rhythm with normal frontal QRS axis
Precordial leads showed low amplitudes and Q waves in leads V1 to V3

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of fever, anosmia, and shortness of breath, combined with the positive nasopharyngeal swab and chest radiography findings, are consistent with COVID-19 pneumonia.
The patient's low oxygen saturation and coarse rales at the lung bases bilaterally suggest acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS).
The patient's symptoms and positive nasopharyngeal swab suggest viral pneumonia.
The patient's history of obstructive sleep apnea and symptoms of shortness of breath and low oxygen saturation suggest obstructive sleep apnea-related respiratory failure.
The patient's symptoms of fever, anosmia, and shortness of breath, combined with the positive nasopharyngeal swab, are consistent with influenza pneumonia.
The patient's symptoms and chest radiography findings suggest community-acquired pneumonia.
The patient's symptoms of shortness of breath and low oxygen saturation suggest respiratory failure.
The patient's symptoms and positive nasopharyngeal swab suggest pneumococcal pneumonia.

rationales.F10: Chest Radiography suggestive of bilateral multifocal pneumonia is consistent with COVID-19 pneumonia and viral pneumonia.
